mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the FEDFUNDS rate above 2.25% for three consecutive months reduces real discount rates, lowering the present value of future earnings for equities and thereby producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in the tightening phase are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) or FEDFUNDS reverts below 2.25% within 2 months, reversing the signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 0.3% for two consecutive months, investors anticipate a faster than expected rate hike path, causing equity discount rates to rise and S&P 500 20-day forward returns to turn negative.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns do not fall below -0.5% in any of the triggered months or CPIAUCSL reverts to below 0.3% within 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in PAYEMS (labor market additions) followed by a sustained decline in UNRATE (unemployment) indicates strengthening labor demand, which raises expected corporate profits and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a month and UNRATE decreases by >0.2% in the following month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) or the PAYEMS/UNRATE relationship reverts to weak correlation (<0.3) within 2 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly INDPRO (industrial production) reading above 105.0 for three consecutive months suggests an expanding supply side, which, when combined with falling UNRATE, creates a supply-driven bull case that supports positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain flat or negative over the 3-month INDPRO expansion period (mean < 0.0%) or UNRATE does not fall meaningfully during the same window.

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (housing starts) surges by more than 15% in a quarter while UNRATE falls by more than 0.5%, it signals a strong housing recovery that boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >15% in a 3-month window and UNRATE decreases by >0.5% over the same period
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns do not exceed +0.8% in any of the triggered quarters or HOUST growth reverses before UNRATE decline is resolved.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in PAYEMS (job additions) for four consecutive months while FEDFUNDS remains below 2.0% suggests a labor market cooling that raises policy patience and reduces growth expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases by >5% each month for 4 consecutive months and FEDFUNDS < 2.0% throughout
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns do not fall below -1.0% during the cooling period or PAYEMS recovers before the FEDFUNDS remains below 2.0% for 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in RSAFS (money supply growth) below -1% for two consecutive months, without a corresponding drop in GDP indicators, signals deflationary pressure that compresses equity valuations and yields negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls below -1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns remain non-negative or RSAFS recovers above -1% within 1 month, failing to sustain the signal.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE remains above 4.0% for three months in a row despite steady GDP growth, it indicates weak labor absorption and potential supply-side bottlenecks, which can lead to higher than expected cost pressures and negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE stays above 4.0% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns do not fall below -0.5% during the high-unemployment period or UNRATE falls below 4.0% within 2 months.
